title: The Queen of Tellico
premise: Greenwater stands on stilts over a drowned town and ties its boats to a steeple. Its winter grain went down the lake on a barge and never came back. The barge is lashed to a gambling boat anchored in plain sight, whose owner is selling the town its own corn by the cup across a faro table and calling it salvage. An old woman with a ladle chained to her wrist wants the grain and wants him hanged, in that order, and she is running out of time for both.

places.name: Greenwater
places.what: Plank streets on stilts, a cook-shed with a line out the door, a steeple standing out of the lake with a bell and a mooring ring

places.name: The Queen of Tellico
places.what: A sternwheeler with a saloon deck, a faro table, a boiler that should not be lit, and the grain barge lashed along her off side

places.name: Hangman's Chute
places.what: The fast water below the old dam: the only way to take a barge home without passing the Queen's guns

stages.set_by: Stepping off the skiff at Greenwater landing with the scoop from Pritchard's desk
stages.log: Greenwater is a town on stilts with a queue from the cook-shed to the water. Everybody in the queue is looking at the same boat.

stages.set_by: Hearing Opal Starnes out at the cook-shed
stages.log: Opal Starnes has corn for nine days and a town for ninety. Her grain is on Lyle Hatcher's boat. She wants it back, and she wants him on the steeple.

stages.set_by: Boarding the Queen of Tellico, by the gangway or over the off side from Rafferty's skiff
stages.log: The Queen of Tellico has a band, a bar and a faro bank. The stake at the high table is a cup of Greenwater's own corn.
Commodore Hatcher deals without looking at his hands. He says the barge is salvage, the law is on his side, and would you care for a card.

stages.set_by: Passing the check on the button 'Deal. The barge against my gun.'
stages.log: You took the barge off Lyle Hatcher with his own deck. He stood the house a round and called it the best hand he ever lost.

stages.set_by: The button 'Cut the barge loose.' and bringing it through Hangman's Chute
stages.log: The grain barge reached Greenwater through Hangman's Chute. Some cargo was lost in the rapids.

stages.set_by: The button 'Burn the occupied Queen.', offered only after Rafferty has said who is aboard
stages.log: The occupied Queen burned with the grain lashed alongside. People tried to reach the water. The cargo is lost; the crew's account still needs witnesses.

stages.set_by: The button 'Sell me a share, Commodore.'
stages.log: You told Greenwater the barge went down in the Chute. Hatcher counted your share onto the felt, and Opal Starnes thanked you for trying.

stages.set_by: Failing the check on the button 'Deal. The barge against my gun.'
stages.log: Lyle Hatcher won your gun on the turn of a card and gave it back with a bow. He says you may still buy in.

stages.set_by: Opening the strongbox under the faro table
stages.log: There is a letter in Hatcher's strongbox. He was paid in stamped silver to hold the grain past first frost. Selling it back was his own idea.
Greenwater rang the steeple bell and hanged Lyle Hatcher from the mooring ring. Opal Starnes held the ladle the whole time.

stages.set_by: The button 'He goes to Pritchard, alive.'
stages.log: Lyle Hatcher left Greenwater in irons in the bottom of a skiff, still talking.

objectives.text: Find who keeps the stores at Greenwater
Get aboard the Queen of Tellico
Get the grain barge off Commodore Hatcher, or get paid
(Optional) Find out why a gambler wanted a town's corn

options.label: Deal. The barge against my gun.
options.now: One hand of cards, with a check of nerve. Win and the barge is yours; lose and you have only lost the stake
options.later: Won: the grain goes home whole and Hatcher owes you nothing but likes you. He can be found at the fair with a boat for hire

options.label: Cut the barge loose.
options.now: The barge escapes through the Chute. Rafferty pilots if alive; otherwise the player steers. Some cargo is lost.
options.later: Greenwater receives the recovered cargo; losses depend on the actual route and pilot state. Hatcher may seek revenge if alive. No fixed fraction or dead pilot is asserted.

options.label: Burn the occupied Queen.
options.now: The occupied Queen and the winter cargo still lashed alongside burn. People are endangered; no exact death count is invented.
options.later: Greenwater loses the grain. Survivors need help, and Belden can offer immediate food without requiring political consent.

options.label: Sell me a share, Commodore.
options.now: You are paid well and Greenwater is told the grain is lost
options.later: The missing grain makes Greenwater vulnerable. Delegate Belden offers real meals and a later provisioning agreement that the town may contest or refuse; a bowl is not a signature.

options.label: He's yours, Opal.
options.later: Hatcher is dead. His testimony is lost, not every witness or document about the payment. Any recovered hire letter remains evidence.

options.label: He goes to Pritchard, alive.
options.now: Hatcher is taken to Mercy Crossing
options.later: He talks at the fair, to anybody who will stand him a drink, about silver with a square mark. Opal does not forgive it

options.label: Let him keep his boat.
options.now: Hatcher sails with the band playing
options.later: He is a friend on the river for the rest of the act, and Greenwater shuts its cook-shed door to you

evidence.found: Hatcher's strongbox, under the faro table on the saloon deck
The Queen's bow, seen from Rafferty's skiff: the chain is rusted through at the third link

ways_through: Cut the barge loose with Rafferty and run the Chute. Needs no card played, no check passed and nothing optional.
Win the barge at Hatcher's table.
Buy a share and tell Greenwater the grain is gone.
cannot_break: If Hatcher is shot at the table his crew fight and the barge can still be cut loose or burned. If Rafferty is dead the player can steer the Chute alone and loses half the grain instead of a third. If Opal Starnes is dead the cook-shed is kept by whoever is next in the queue and no hanging is asked for. If the player leaves without doing anything the road stays unresolved: the barge stays with the Queen and nothing is settled by the fair being called.

open_questions: Resolved 2026-11-16: the drowned settlement stays fictional; real historical claims are to be verified separately before publication (decision 14).
Resolved by packet 2: stage 42 is the completed Chute escape and stage 43 the fire that takes the occupied boat and the cargo lashed to it. They are alternatives; there is no cut-then-burn.

Resolved by packet 3: no fixed fraction of the cargo is asserted in the journal, in Rafferty's line or in the consequence text, and a dead Rafferty does not speak. The living and dead pilot's difference in loss stays a mechanical rule in cannot_break until a route is measured.
Open for Iris: whether Opal Starnes's illness is something the player can learn and act on.
